title_vi: Các tầng bộ nhớ, đo trên một máy: thanh ghi, bộ đệm, bộ nhớ chính, đĩa, mạng

source_snapshot.note: Pinned commit/path body read from a partial clone of the source repository; git hash-object of the retrieved body matches the source-map blob. No source-image bytes used.

related.reason_vi: Vì sao ghi nối tiếp và gom thay đổi lại rẻ hơn trên đĩa.
Kafka dựa vào page cache của hệ điều hành.
Cùng cách đo trên một máy khác, kèm giải nghĩa tên các loại bộ nhớ và ổ lưu trữ.

claims.evidence: The Linux v6.18 documentation for CPU cache attributes in sysfs, the block queue rotational attribute and transparent huge pages was read from a partial clone of torvalds/linux; the latencies were measured by the author, who ran a C pointer-chasing program (gcc 13.3, -O2), O_DIRECT random reads and curl requests on a four-vCPU virtual machine on 2026-10-18.

mobile.evidence: Chromium (Playwright) rendered lesson.md (markdown-it, tables enabled, every <details> open, a 16 px page gutter) at each width: the page never scrolled sideways and the figure was scaled to the column; the smallest SVG font-size times that scale is the recorded minimum at 320 px. `python3 -m scripts.figures check --browser` measured every line of the figure in Chromium inside its box. Not GitHub, not a real phone and not learner testing.

claims.claim_vi: The kernel exposes CPU cache parameters (level, type, size, coherency line size) under /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cache/index*; the block queue attribute rotational states whether the device is of rotational type.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of torvalds/linux at tag v6.18 (commit 7d0a66e4bb9081d75c82ec4957c50034cb0ea449).

claims.claim_vi: With huge pages a TLB miss runs faster, especially with virtualization and nested page tables, and a single TLB entry maps more memory, so there are fewer TLB misses.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of torvalds/linux at tag v6.18 (commit 7d0a66e4bb9081d75c82ec4957c50034cb0ea449).

claims.claim_vi: Measured on a 4-vCPU VM (sysfs: L1d 32 KiB, L2 1 MiB, L3 33 MiB, 64-byte lines), across saved runs: a dependent add 0.4 ns; one dependent read in a random cycle over 16 KiB 1.5-1.7 ns, 256 KiB 4.4-5.0 ns, 1 MiB 15-17 ns, 4 MiB 145-152 ns, 64 MiB 165-180 ns, 1 GiB 326-409 ns; in one back-to-back pair, 1 GiB took 326 ns with 4 KiB pages and 225 ns with MADV_HUGEPAGE; 3,000 random 4 KiB O_DIRECT reads of a 2 GiB file averaged 72 us, worst 2.1 ms, on a disk the kernel reports as rotational; ten HTTPS requests to GitHub through the environment's proxy took a median of about 60 ms from TLS completion to first byte and a median of 0.27 s each including connection setup.
claims.verified_by: The author ran and measured this on 2026-10-18; outputs saved per run (memlat.out, memlat2.out, memlat2_huge.out, sweep.out, curl.out); runs varied by up to about a quarter at 1 GiB.

claims.claim_vi: The source states: Memory types vary by speed, size and function: registers inside the CPU, caches close to the CPU, main memory (RAM), SSDs, HDDs and remote secondary storage for backup and archiving.

design_notes_vi: Hai khung bậc đo (trong bộ xử lý và bộ nhớ; đĩa và mạng) và một khung đọc con số. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: The source describes six memory types; the lesson measures one read at each level on the authoring machine, merges SSD and HDD into one virtual disk, and uses an HTTPS request as the network tier.

The lesson adds two measured observations the source does not make: a cache level reported by the hardware did not show in the measurement, and main-memory latency depends on address translation (huge pages).
editorial_note_vi: Bài mới viết trong kho này, chờ review kỹ thuật. Chưa user testing hoặc phê duyệt phát hành.
